newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa c.bank no immediate plans to quit fwd mkt.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa c.bank no immediate plans to quit fwd mkt.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank has no immediate plans to withdraw from the forward rand market, deputy governor James Cross said, reacting to rumours which helped send the currency sharply lower on Tuesday.

"No, we have no immediate plans (to withdraw from the forward market). The only thing we might consider in time is maybe changing our pricing strategy, but that doesn't mean we can pull out of the market in the near term," Cross told Reuters by telephone from Pretoria.

Earlier, traders said the rand had come under attack, in part on rumours that the cenrtral bank was planning a rapid withdrawal from the market. The talk appeared to have been sparked by a meeting on Tuesday morning between Cross and traders, they said.
However, Cross said the discussions had been only of a general and exploratory nature.
The Reserve Bank has said on many occasions that it wants to withdraw eventually from the forward cover market and see private institutions take on an increasing role in making a market.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said last week that the central bank's forward foreign exchange position had risen to $20 billion but was likely to decline rapidly in 1997. He told a parliamentary media briefing that after climbing from $8 billion last year, the forward cover book was expected to start falling rapidly this year.
Stals said he hoped that the Reserve Bank would be able to change the way in which it made forward cover available in the market in future.
The book is managed on behalf of the Department of Finance and any losses are therefore borne by the taxpayer.
